newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: FORECAST - Yields seen rising on Portugal 5-yr bonds.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Yields seen rising on Portugal 5-yr bonds.

text.p: Yields were seen rising to around 6.5 percent, from the secondary market level of 6.4 percent, at the Institute for Public Credit Management's (IGCP) offer of 25 billion escudos of five-year bonds on Tuesday, analysts said.
As a result of the increase in yields, the IGCP might accept bids for only part of the offer or even reject all bids at the sale, they said.
The average yield was 5.94 percent on the previous sale of March 2002 paper on February 25. Results of the auction are due around 1100 GMT.
"The bulk of demand should be between 6.45 and 6.55 percent but the IGCP may set the cut off at 6.50 percent," said one analyst.

"(Today) is not a good day to go (to the auction) with low yields because the Bank of Portugal is not expected to cut rates and the Fed (U.S. Federal Reserve) should increase its rates 25 basis points," said another analyst.
The Fed is widely excpected to announce a tightening at its Open Market Committee meeting later on Tuesday.
